This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

--- # goimports-reviser ![logo](./images/reviser-muscot_200.png) Tool for Golang to sort goimports by 3-4 groups: std, general, company (optional), and project dependencies. Also formats your code (no need to use `gofmt` or `goimports` separately). ## Features - Sort imports into logical groups (stdlib, general, company, project) - Remove unused imports with `-rm-unused` - Set aliases for versioned packages with `-set-alias` - Format code automatically with `-format` - Apply to directories recursively - Group company imports separately with `-company-prefixes` ## Usage ### Basic command: ```bash goimports-reviser -rm-unused -set-alias -format ./reviser/reviser.go ``` ### Apply to a directory recursively: ```bash goimports-reviser -rm-unused -set-alias -format -recursive reviser ``` ### Apply to all files: ```bash goimports-reviser -rm-unused -set-alias -format ./... ``` ### Apply to multiple targets: ```bash goimports-reviser -rm-unused -set-alias -format ./reviser/reviser.go ./pkg/... ``` ### Options: ```text Usage of goimports-reviser: -apply-to-generated-files Apply imports sorting and formatting(if the option is set) to generated files. Generated file is a file with first comment which starts with comment '// Code generated'. Optional parameter. -company-prefixes string Company package prefixes which will be placed after 3rd-party group by default(if defined). Values should be comma-separated. Optional parameters. -excludes string Exclude files or dirs, example: '.git/,proto/*.go'. -file-path string Deprecated. Put file name as an argument(last item) of command line. -format Option will perform additional formatting. Optional parameter. -imports-order string Your imports groups can be sorted in your way. std - std import group; general - libs for general purpose; company - inter-org or your company libs(if you set '-company-prefixes'-option, then 4th group will be split separately. In other case, it will be the part of general purpose libs); project - your local project dependencies; blanked - imports with "_" alias; dotted - imports with "." alias. Optional parameter. (default "std,general,company,project") -list-diff Option will list files whose formatting differs from goimports-reviser. Optional parameter. -local string Deprecated -output string Can be "file", "write" or "stdout". Whether to write the formatted content back to the file or to stdout. When "write" together with "-list-diff" will list the file name and write back to the file. Optional parameter. (default "file") -project-name string Your project name(ex.: github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser). Optional parameter. -recursive Apply rules recursively if target is a directory. In case of ./... execution will be recursively applied by default. Optional parameter. -rm-unused Remove unused imports. Optional parameter. -separate-named Separate named imports from their group with a new line. Optional parameter. -set-alias Set alias for versioned package names, like 'github.com/go-pg/pg/v9'. In this case import will be set as 'pg "github.com/go-pg/pg/v9"'. Optional parameter. -set-exit-status set the exit status to 1 if a change is needed/made. Optional parameter. -use-cache Use cache to improve performance. Optional parameter. -version Show version. ``` ## Examples ### Before usage: ```go package testdata import ( "log" "github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/testdata/innderpkg" "bytes" "golang.org/x/exp/slices" ) ``` ### After usage: ```go package testdata import ( "bytes" "log" "golang.org/x/exp/slices" "github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/testdata/innderpkg" ) ``` Comments for imports are preserved: ```go package testdata import ( "fmt" // comments to the package here ) ``` ### Example with `-company-prefixes` option Before: ```go package testdata // goimports-reviser/testdata import ( "fmt" //fmt package "golang.org/x/exp/slices" //custom package "github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/pkg" // this is a company package which is not a part of the project, but is a part of your organization "goimports-reviser/pkg" ) ``` After: ```go package testdata // goimports-revis 3236 characters elided file is a file with first comment which starts with comment '// Code generated'. Usage of ./executable:
  -apply-to-generated-files
    	Apply imports sorting and formatting(if the option is set) to generated files. Generated file is a file with first comment which starts with comment '// Code generated'. Optional parameter.
  -company-prefixes string
    	Company package prefixes which will be placed after 3rd-party group by default(if defined). Values should be comma-separated. Optional parameters.
  -excludes string
    	Exclude files or dirs, example: '.git/,proto/*.go'.
  -file-path string
    	Deprecated. Put file name as an argument(last item) of command line.
  -format
    	Option will perform additional formatting. Optional parameter.
  -imports-order string
    	Your imports groups can be sorted in your way. 
    	std - std import group; 
    	general - libs for general purpose; 
    	company - inter-org or your company libs(if you set '-company-prefixes'-option, then 4th group will be split separately. In other case, it will be the part of general purpose libs); 
    	project - your local project dependencies;
    	blanked - imports with "_" alias;
    	dotted - imports with "." alias.
    	Optional parameter. (default "std,general,company,project")
  -list-diff
    	Option will list files whose formatting differs from goimports-reviser. Optional parameter.
  -local string
    	Deprecated
  -output string
    	Can be "file", "write" or "stdout". Whether to write the formatted content back to the file or to stdout. When "write" together with "-list-diff" will list the file name and write back to the file. Optional parameter. (default "file")
  -project-name string
    	Your project name(ex.: github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser). Optional parameter.
  -recursive
    	Apply rules recursively if target is a directory. In case of ./... execution will be recursively applied by default. Optional parameter.
  -rm-unused
    	Remove unused imports. Optional parameter.
  -separate-named
    	Option will separate named imports from the rest of the imports, per group. Optional parameter.
  -set-alias
    	Set alias for versioned package names, like 'github.com/go-pg/pg/v9'. In this case import will be set as 'pg "github.com/go-pg/pg/v9"'. Optional parameter.
  -set-exit-status
    	set the exit status to 1 if a change is needed/made. Optional parameter.
  -use-cache
    	Use cache to improve performance. Optional parameter.
  -version
    	Show version information
  -version-only
    	Show only the version string

    print("----")

import os
print(os.getcwd())

--- # goimports-reviser ![logo](./images/reviser-muscot_200.png) Tool for Golang to sort goimports by 3-4 groups: std, general, company (optional), and project dependencies. Also formats your code (no need to use `gofmt` or `goimports` separately). ## Features - Sort imports into logical groups (stdlib, general, company, project) - Remove unused imports with `-rm-unused` - Set aliases for versioned packages with `-set-alias` - Format code automatically with `-format` - Apply to directories recursively - Group company imports separately with `-company-prefixes` ## Usage ### Basic command: ```bash goimports-reviser -rm-unused -set-alias -format ./reviser/reviser.go ``` ### Apply to a directory recursively: ```bash goimports-reviser -rm-unused -set-alias -format -recursive reviser ``` ### Apply to all files: ```bash goimports-reviser -rm-unused -set-alias -format ./... ``` ### Apply to multiple targets: ```bash goimports-reviser -rm-unused -set-alias -format ./reviser/reviser.go ./pkg/... ``` ### Options: ```text Usage of goimports-reviser: -apply-to-generated-files Apply imports sorting and formatting(if the option is set) to generated files. Generated file is a file with first comment which starts with comment '// Code generated'. Optional parameter. -company-prefixes string Company package prefixes which will be placed after 3rd-party group by default(if defined). Values should be comma-separated. Optional parameters. -excludes string Exclude files or dirs, example: '.git/,proto/*.go'. -file-path string Deprecated. Put file name as an argument(last item) of command line. -format Option will perform additional formatting. Optional parameter. -imports-order string Your imports groups can be sorted in your way. std - std import group; general - libs for general purpose; company - inter-org or your company libs(if you set '-company-prefixes'-option, then 4th group will be split separately. In other case, it will be the part of general purpose libs); project - your local project dependencies; blanked - imports with "_" alias; dotted - imports with "." alias. Optional parameter. (default "std,general,company,project") -list-diff Option will list files whose formatting differs from goimports-reviser. Optional parameter. -local string Deprecated -output string Can be "file", "write" or "stdout". Whether to write the formatted content back to the file or to stdout. When "write" together with "-list-diff" will list the file name and write back to the file. Optional parameter. (default "file") -project-name string Your project name(ex.: github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser). Optional parameter. -recursive Apply rules recursively if target is a directory. In case of ./... execution will be recursively applied by default. Optional parameter. -rm-unused Remove unused imports. Optional parameter. -separate-named Separate named imports from their group with a new line. Optional parameter. -set-alias Set alias for versioned package names, like 'github.com/go-pg/pg/v9'. In this case import will be set as 'pg "github.com/go-pg/pg/v9"'. Optional parameter. -set-exit-status set the exit status to 1 if a change is needed/made. Optional parameter. -use-cache Use cache to improve performance. func init() {
	stdPkgs = loadStd()

func loadStd() map[string]bool {
	m := make(map[string]bool)
	cmd := exec.Command("go", "list", "std")
	out, err := cmd.Output()
	if err == nil {
		for _, l := range strings.Split(string(out), "\n") {
			l = strings.TrimSpace(l)
			if l != "" {
				m[l] = true
			}
		}
		if len(m) > 0 {
			return m
		}
	}
	fallback := []string{"bytes", "fmt", "os", "log", "strings", "strconv", "errors", "io", "net/http", "encoding/json", "context", "sync", "time", "math", "sort", "path/filepath", "os/exec", "crypto/md5", "encoding/hex", "go/ast", "go/format", "go/parser", "go/token", "flag", "regexp", "path", "unicode", "unicode/utf8", "reflect", "testing"}
	for _, p := range fallback {
		m[p] = true
	}
	return m
}

func isStd(path string) bool {
	return stdPkgs[path]
}

var generatedRe = regexp.MustCompile(`^// Code generated .* DO NOT EDIT\.$`)

func isGenerated(fset *token.FileSet, f *ast.File) bool {
	for _, cg := range f.Comments {
		// only consider comments before package clause?
		// f.Package is offset of "package" keyword
		if cg.End() > f.Package {
			// Actually need to check if comment is before package: compare positions
			// Use fset position
			cpos := fset.Position(cg.Pos())
			ppos := fset.Position(f.Package)
			if cpos.Line > ppos.Line {
				continue
			}
			// if same line? package on same line as comment? unlikely
			if cpos.Filename != ppos.Filename {
				continue
			}
		}
		for _, c := range cg.List {
			txt := strings.TrimSpace(c.Text)
			// only // comments, not /* */
			if !strings.HasPrefix(txt, "//") {
				continue
			}
			// c.Text is like "// Code generated ..." without leading spaces? parser trims? Actually Text includes "//" exactly.
			// Need to check without leading spaces (already trimmed)
			if generatedRe.MatchString(txt) {
				return true
			}
		}
	}
	return false
}

func getProjectName(providedPath, flagProject string) (string, error) {
	if flagProject != "" {
		return flagProject, nil
	}
	abs, err := filepath.Abs(providedPath)
	if err != nil {
		abs = providedPath
	}
	dir := filepath.Dir(abs)
	for {
		gomod := filepath.Join(dir, "go.mod")
		data, err := os.ReadFile(gomod)
		if err == nil {
			// parse module line
			for _, line := range strings.Split(string(data), "\n") {
				line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
				if strings.HasPrefix(line, "module") {
					rest := strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(line, "module"))
					// rest may be quoted? handle
					rest = strings.TrimSpace(rest)
					if rest == "" {
						return "", fmt.Errorf("module is undefined")
					}
					// remove quotes if any
					if len(rest) >= 2 && ((rest[0] == '"' && rest[len(rest)-1] == '"') || (rest[0] == '\'' && rest[len(rest)-1] == '\'')) {
						rest, _ = strconv.Unquote(rest)
						if rest == "" {
							return "", fmt.Errorf("module is undefined")
						}
					} else {
						// take first field
						fields := strings.Fields(rest)
						if len(fields) == 0 {
							return "", fmt.Errorf("module is undefined")
						}
						rest = fields[0]
					}
					if rest == "" {
						return "", fmt.Errorf("module is undefined")
					}
					return rest, nil
				}
			}
			return "", fmt.Errorf("module is undefined")
		}
		parent := filepath.Dir(dir)
		if parent == dir {
			break
		}
		dir = parent
	}
	return "", fmt.Errorf("open go.mod: no such file or directory")
}

func matchPrefix(path, prefix string) bool {
	p := strings.TrimSuffix(prefix, "/")
	if p == "" {
		return false
	}
	if path == p {
		return true
	}
	return strings.HasPrefix(path, p+"/")
}

func classify(path, alias, project string, companies []string, hasBlanked, hasDotted bool) string {
	if alias == "_" && hasBlanked {
		return "blanked"
	}
	if alias == "." && hasDotted {
		return "dotted"
	}
	if project != "" && matchPrefix(path, project) {
		return "project"
	}
	for _, c := range companies {
		if matchPrefix(path, c) {
			return "company"
		}
	}
	if isStd(path) {
		return "std"
	}
	return "general"
}

	Alias   string
	Comment string // trailing comment text including // or /* */? Actually full group text?
	RawPath string // quoted string as in source, e.g. "\"fmt\""
	OrigComment *ast.CommentGroup

func isVersioned(path string) bool {
	// check ends with /vN where N is digits
	idx := strings.LastIndex(path, "/")
	if idx < 0 {
		return false
	}
	suffix := path[idx+1:]
	if len(suffix) < 2 || suffix[0] != 'v' {
		return false
	}
	for _, ch := range suffix[1:] {
		if ch < '0' || ch > '9' {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}

func getPkgName(importPath, dir string) (string, error) {

	cmd.Dir = dir
	out, err := cmd.Output()
	if err != nil {
		// go list returns 0 even with Incomplete? Actually it returns 0, but JSON contains Error
		// If exec fails, return err
		return "", err
	}
	// parse JSON to get Name and Error
	var res struct {
		Name  string `json:"Name"`
		Error *struct {
			Err string `json:"Err"`
		} `json:"Error"`
		Dir        string `json:"Dir"`
		ImportPath string `json:"ImportPath"`
	}
	// go list with single package returns single JSON object, not array
	// But with -e -json, it may return multiple? For single, one object.
	dec := jsonDecoder(out)
	if err := dec.Decode(&res); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	if res.Error != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("%s", res.Error.Err)

	return res.Name, nil

	needGlobal := singleCount > 1 && *outputFlag == "stdout" && *listDiff
	if needGlobal {
		// Global handling for multiple singles with stdout+list-diff
		type res struct {
			provided  string
			abs       string
			formatted string
			changed   bool
		}
		var results []res

		for idx, p := range paths {

			results = append(results, res{p, abs, formatted, changed})
